framework.name: Quality Teaching Tool
framework.source: Indicator codes and names: ECDA QTT Guidebook (Appendix A of the Tend PRD). Level descriptors and look-fors are Tend DRAFTS in our own words, pending Agape curriculum review and ECDA permission (PRD risk: QTT licensing).

levels.1: Basic positive practice
levels.2: More responsive and intentional
levels.3: Advanced facilitation, child-led, more peer involvement

indicators.name: Creating a Warm, Safe and Motivating Environment

levels.1: Greets children warmly and keeps the space safe and calm.
levels.2: Adjusts tone, space and routines so each child feels welcome and wants to take part.
levels.3: Children help shape a caring space and look out for each other's comfort and safety.

look_fors: Greets children by name with warmth
Children move about confidently and seek out the educator

indicators.name: Facilitating Responsive Interactions

levels.1: Notices and acknowledges children's bids for attention.
levels.2: Responds promptly and in tune with each child's cues and mood.
levels.3: Follows children's lead and builds long, back-and-forth exchanges from their interests.

look_fors: Gets down to child's eye level
Responds to a child's bid within moments
Builds on what the child says or shows

indicators.name: Facilitating Reciprocal Interactions

levels.1: Takes turns in simple exchanges with children.
levels.2: Keeps conversations going with pauses that invite children to contribute.
levels.3: Children sustain multi-turn conversations with the educator and with each other.

look_fors: Invites a second child to join the exchange

indicators.name: Supporting Children Through Challenges

levels.1: Comforts children who are upset and keeps them safe.
levels.2: Names the difficulty and offers a strategy to try.
levels.3: Coaches children to work through challenges themselves and support peers.

look_fors: Acknowledges the child's feeling before redirecting
Lets the child try again with support

indicators.name: Engaging in Inclusive and Respectful Interactions

levels.1: Speaks respectfully to every child and avoids favouritism.
levels.2: Adapts interactions so every child, including quieter ones, is included.
levels.3: Children show respect and include one another without prompting.

look_fors: Uses each child's name and preferred language
Draws quieter children into the activity
Responds to all children with equal warmth

indicators.name: Developing Values

levels.1: Names values such as kindness or honesty during routines.
levels.2: Plans moments that let children explore what a value looks like.
levels.3: Children discuss values and apply them to real situations in class.

look_fors: Talks about a value in context
Uses stories or role play to explore values
Asks children what a kind choice would be

indicators.name: Reinforcing Values

levels.1: Praises behaviour that shows a value.
levels.2: Gives specific feedback linking the action to the value.
levels.3: Children recognise and affirm values in each other's actions.

look_fors: Links behaviour to its effect on others
Children notice kind acts by peers

indicators.name: Encouraging Awareness, Respect and Celebration of Diversity

levels.1: Uses materials that show different cultures and families.
levels.2: Invites children to share and compare their own traditions.
levels.3: Children explore differences with curiosity and celebrate them together.

look_fors: Books and materials reflect diverse families
Invites children to share home languages or customs
Responds positively to questions about difference

indicators.name: Helping Children Build Positive Self-Concept

levels.1: Acknowledges children's efforts and achievements.
levels.2: Highlights each child's strengths and growth over time.
levels.3: Children describe their own strengths and set small goals.

look_fors: Displays children's work with their words
Asks children what they are proud of

indicators.name: Helping Children Identify Emotions

levels.1: Names emotions children show.
levels.2: Helps children notice body cues and name a wider range of feelings.
levels.3: Children name their own and others' feelings in daily situations.

look_fors: Asks 'how do you think he feels?'

indicators.name: Helping Children Express Emotions

levels.1: Accepts children's feelings without dismissing them.
levels.2: Offers safe ways to express feelings through words, art or movement.
levels.3: Children choose appropriate ways to express feelings on their own.

look_fors: Validates feelings ('it's OK to feel sad')
Provides a calm corner or expression tools

indicators.name: Helping Children Self-Manage and Regulate Emotions

levels.1: Calms children who are upset.
levels.2: Teaches simple calming strategies and prompts their use.
levels.3: Children use calming strategies independently and help peers.

look_fors: Prompts a strategy before stepping in

indicators.name: Helping Children Identify and Respond to Emotions and Perspectives of Others

levels.1: Points out how others might feel.
levels.2: Asks children to consider another's view and how to respond.
levels.3: Children show empathy and respond to peers' feelings unprompted.

look_fors: Guides children to comfort a peer

levels.1: Encourages sharing and taking turns.
levels.2: Sets up activities that need cooperation and helping.
levels.3: Children cooperate, share and help without adult prompting.

indicators.name: Promoting Social Awareness

levels.1: Talks about people and roles in the community.
levels.2: Connects classroom life to families and the wider community.
levels.3: Children take part in projects that contribute to their community.

look_fors: Children plan a way to help others

indicators.name: Developing Perseverance

levels.1: Encourages children to keep trying.
levels.2: Breaks tasks into steps and celebrates persistence.
levels.3: Children take on challenges and keep going through setbacks.

look_fors: Says 'try another way' rather than solving it

indicators.name: Fostering Reflectiveness

levels.1: Asks children what they did.
levels.2: Asks children how they did it and what they might change.
levels.3: Children review their own work and plan improvements.

look_fors: Children revisit and revise their work

indicators.name: Helping Children Appreciate Perspectives and Contributions of Others

levels.1: Lets children share ideas in turn.
levels.2: Highlights how different ideas help the group.
levels.3: Children build on each other's ideas and credit peers.

look_fors: Invites several children to share ideas
Connects one child's idea to another's
Children say 'I like your idea because…'

levels.1: Provides open-ended materials.
levels.2: Invites children to try new ways of using materials and ideas.
levels.3: Children design, invent and test their own creations.

levels.1: Responds positively to children's questions.
levels.2: Sets up provocations that spark wondering.
levels.3: Children pose their own questions and investigate them.

indicators.name: Promoting Engagement and Interest

levels.1: Gets children's attention for activities.
levels.2: Builds activities around children's interests to sustain engagement.
levels.3: Children stay deeply involved and extend activities themselves.

look_fors: Children stay on task for sustained periods

indicators.name: Making Connections Through an Integrated Approach

levels.1: Links an activity to one other learning area.
levels.2: Plans experiences that connect several learning areas around a theme.
levels.3: Children make their own connections across learning areas and to real life.

look_fors: Activity links two or more learning areas
Children connect ideas to home or community

indicators.name: Catering to Diverse Learners

levels.1: Notices that children learn differently.
levels.2: Plans different entry points and supports for different learners.
levels.3: Children choose ways of learning that suit them.

look_fors: Includes visual, verbal and hands-on options

indicators.name: Managing and Maximising Learning Opportunities

levels.1: Keeps routines running with little waiting time.
levels.2: Uses transitions and routines as chances to learn.
levels.3: Children manage routines themselves, freeing time for deeper learning.

look_fors: Children know what to do next

indicators.name: Providing Various Types of Learning Experiences

levels.1: Offers a mix of group and individual activities.
levels.2: Balances adult-guided and child-initiated experiences on purpose.
levels.3: Children move between experiences of their choice with purpose.

look_fors: Mix of whole-group, small-group and individual time

indicators.name: Establishing Clear Expectations and Guiding Proactively

levels.1: States rules simply and reminds children of them.
levels.2: Sets expectations with reasons and guides before problems arise.
levels.3: Children help set expectations and remind each other.

look_fors: Explains the reason behind a rule

indicators.name: Modifying Instruction to Meet Children's Needs

levels.1: Repeats or simplifies when children are unsure.
levels.2: Changes pace, materials or grouping in the moment based on responses.
levels.3: Children's responses and ideas visibly change the direction of the lesson.

look_fors: Changes approach when children lose interest
Follows a child's idea into the next step

indicators.name: Exercising Flexibility in Catering to Children's Needs and Interests

levels.1: Allows small changes to plans when children ask.
levels.2: Adapts plans around children's emerging interests.
levels.3: Children's interests drive extended projects.

look_fors: Adjusts the plan to an emerging interest
Extends time when engagement is high

indicators.name: Empowering Children's Independence

levels.1: Lets children do simple tasks for themselves.
levels.2: Sets up the space and routines so children can manage on their own.
levels.3: Children take charge of tasks and support others' independence.

look_fors: Waits before stepping in to help

indicators.name: Encouraging Children to Make Choices and Decisions

levels.1: Offers simple choices between two options.
levels.2: Gives meaningful choices and talks through decisions.
levels.3: Children make and justify group and individual decisions.

look_fors: Asks children to explain their choice
Children vote or agree on group decisions

indicators.name: Providing Children Opportunities to Lead and Take on Roles

levels.1: Assigns simple helper roles.
levels.2: Rotates leadership roles and coaches children in them.
levels.3: Children lead activities and take on roles they design.

look_fors: Children lead a part of an activity

indicators.name: Engaging Children Through a Variety of Play

levels.1: Provides time and materials for play.
levels.2: Joins play to extend it without taking over.
levels.3: Children sustain complex play with rich roles and ideas.

look_fors: Variety of play types (pretend, construction, physical)
Educator joins play as a co-player

indicators.name: Catering to Children's Level of Engagement

levels.1: Notices when children are disengaged.
levels.2: Adjusts challenge or support to re-engage individual children.
levels.3: Children self-regulate their engagement and choose challenges.

look_fors: Offers extensions for children who finish early

levels.1: Talks with children throughout the day.
levels.2: Models and introduces new words in context.
levels.3: Children use rich and new vocabulary in their own talk.

indicators.name: Extending the Use of Language Through Print

levels.1: Points out print in the environment.
levels.2: Uses print purposefully with children, such as labels, lists and stories.
levels.3: Children create and use print for their own purposes.

look_fors: Labels and print at child height
Children make signs, lists or books

indicators.name: Encouraging Communication and Conversations

levels.1: Invites children to talk about their experiences.
levels.2: Sets up pair and small-group talk.
levels.3: Children hold sustained conversations with peers.

look_fors: Children respond to each other, not only the adult

indicators.name: Extending Thinking Through Questioning

levels.1: Asks questions, mostly closed or recall questions.
levels.2: Asks open questions and waits for children to think.
levels.3: Uses follow-up questions to deepen thinking, and children ask each other questions.

look_fors: Waits at least 3 seconds after asking
Follows up with 'what makes you think that?'

indicators.name: Providing Support to Deepen Thinking

levels.1: Gives hints when children are stuck.
levels.2: Scaffolds with prompts, models and materials.
levels.3: Children reason aloud and test ideas with light support.

look_fors: Scaffolds instead of giving the answer

indicators.name: Providing Feedback That Extends Understanding and Deepens Thinking

levels.1: Gives general praise such as 'good job'.
levels.2: Gives specific feedback about what the child did.
levels.3: Gives feedback that prompts the child to think further and improve.

look_fors: Feedback ends with a question or next step

levels.1: Presents simple problems with one answer.
levels.2: Sets open problems with more than one solution.
levels.3: Children identify problems themselves and plan solutions.

indicators.name: Engaging Children in Problem Solving

levels.1: Solves problems with children step by step.
levels.2: Guides children to try, check and change their approach.
levels.3: Children solve problems together and explain their strategies.

look_fors: Asks children to predict and test
Children work together on a solution

levels.1: Reminds children of routines and steps.
levels.2: Uses visual schedules and checklists children can follow.
levels.3: Children manage their own belongings, time and tasks.

indicators.name: Facilitating Self-Regulation Skills

levels.1: Tells children to wait or stop.
levels.2: Uses games and strategies that practise waiting and impulse control.
levels.3: Children regulate their behaviour and help peers do so.

look_fors: Gives a strategy before a waiting time
Children remind each other of agreements

levels.1: Gives one instruction at a time.
levels.2: Plays games that ask children to remember and use information.
levels.3: Children hold multi-step plans in mind and carry them out.

levels.1: Shows that there can be more than one way.
levels.2: Asks children to switch rules or think of alternatives.
levels.3: Children shift strategies and see others' viewpoints easily.

indicators.name: Guiding Children in Planning and Organising to Achieve a Goal

levels.1: Tells children the plan for an activity.
levels.2: Helps children make a simple plan and check progress.
levels.3: Children set goals, plan steps and review their own progress.

look_fors: Children draw or say their plan
Children check progress against their plan
